road.title: At the restaurant
road.description: A round and unhurried shape under a hat that has seen service, sitting on a trunk they will not discuss. Tabitha is a Table Broker and deals in reservations and can get you the window at eight, provided you do not ask how.

openObjectives.prompt: Tabitha is guarding a large book in which, it appears, tables are kept. Tell Tabitha that you would like to book a table, using Italian.
Tell Tabitha what you will have to start with, using Italian.

character.name: Tabitha Tuffet
character.description: A round and unhurried shape under a hat that has seen service, sitting on a trunk they will not discuss. Tabitha is a Table Broker and deals in reservations and can get you the window at eight, provided you do not ask how.

npc.narrative: It is alba, and a light pioggia falls on The Absent Copse, which has no alberi and is touchy about it. Tabitha Tuffet stands in a fila of one, beside a piccolo tavolo and a very thick libro. She looks at you, counts, and writes something down with a sharp matita.
npc.native: Buongiorno! Sono Tabitha Tuffet. Il mio lavoro è prenotare tavoli, anche con la pioggia. Oggi voglio prenotare una finestra per otto persone. Tu hai fame stamattina?
npc.translation: Good morning! I am Tabitha Tuffet. My job is to book tables, even in the rain. Today I want to book a window for eight people. Are you hungry this morning?

player: Buongiorno Tabitha! Sì, ho molta fame. Vorrei prenotare un tavolo per due, per favore.

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely start! You greeted Tabitha, said you were hungry, and politely asked to book a table for two, all in correct Italian.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done: you said you would like to book a table, in your own Italian words.

vocabularyEvidence.evidence: Vorrei prenotare un tavolo per due

objectiveResults.feedback: Not yet: this one is about telling Tabitha what you will have to start with. Tabitha will ask you again later.
Not yet: this one is about telling Tabitha that the food is cold or too salty. It will come up again later.

openObjectives.prompt: Tell Tabitha what you will have to start with, using Italian.
Tabitha asks whether everything is all right, in the voice of someone who expects it to be. Tell Tabitha that the food is cold, or too salty, using Italian.

npc.narrative: The pioggia drums on the awning while Tabitha writes your name in a small quaderno, then looks at it as if it might be someone else's. Three passanti go by in the grey light, and she nods, satisfied. A finestra above the stall is steamed over, which she says is a good sign.
npc.native: Un tavolo per due, va bene. Io ho fame con la pioggia: come antipasto prendo il pane, e come primo prendo la zuppa. Tu che cosa prendi?
npc.translation: A table for two, all right. I am hungry in the rain: as a starter I take the bread, and as a first course I take the soup. What do you take?

player: Per cominciare prendo la bruschetta. E poi la pasta, forse.

correction.text: Come antipasto prendo la bruschetta. E come primo prendo la pasta, forse.
correction.translation: As a starter I'll have the bruschetta. And as a first course I'll have the pasta, maybe.

verdict.overallFeedback: Nice work: your Italian is clear, and you told Tabitha you'd have bruschetta and then maybe pasta. Next time, try naming the course with \"come ...\" as Tabitha did.

objectiveResults.feedback: You told Tabitha what you'll have, which is lovely, but "Per cominciare" isn't the wanted phrase; say "come antipasto" for the starter or "come primo" for the first course.
Not yet asked for here: later, tell Tabitha that the food is cold or too salty. We'll come back to this one.

correction.text: Come antipasto prendo la bruschetta. E come primo prendo la pasta, forse.
correction.translation: As a starter I'll have the bruschetta. And as a first course I'll have the pasta, maybe.

openObjectives.prompt: Tabitha asks whether everything is all right, in the voice of someone who expects it to be. Tell Tabitha that the food is cold, or too salty, using Italian.

npc.narrative: Tabitha writes your ordine on a small foglio, using a matita of great seriousness. Fuori, the pioggia keeps up on the strada, and she counts the passanti under the portico: quattro. She seems personally let down.
npc.native: Forse è una buona parola, la uso anch'io con i clienti. Io non voglio mai il pane freddo, e il brodo salato non mi piace. Che cosa bevi con la pasta?
npc.translation: Maybe is a good word, I use it too with my clients. I never want cold bread, and I do not like salty broth. What do you drink with the pasta?

player: Bevo acqua. Ma scusa, la zuppa è fredda! E troppo salata.

verdict.overallFeedback: You answered Tabitha's question about drinks and then politely complained about the soup, all in correct Italian. Great work!

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done: you told Tabitha the soup is cold and too salty, with the right endings (fredda, salata) to match zuppa.

npc.narrative: The cameriere sets down the tavolo's only candela and leaves at once, the way people leave a bad idea. Tabitha lifts the lid of the bowl and regards it with grande sospetto. Outside, the pioggia keeps falling on the piazza.
npc.native: Hai ragione, la zuppa è fredda. Anche il brodo è troppo salato, io non mi fido mai di un brodo. Oggi passano dieci persone sotto la pioggia, e dieci è un numero pari: non mi piace. Che cosa mangi adesso?
npc.translation: You are right, the soup is cold. The broth is also too salty, and I never trust a broth. Today ten people pass by in the rain, and ten is an even number: I do not like it. What are you eating now?

player: Adesso niente, la zuppa è fredda! Haha. Perché non ti piace il numero dieci?

npc.narrative: Tabitha lowers her ombrello and counts the passanti on the strada, lips moving. Behind her a fila of one has formed, which is her own. The pioggia goes on, leggera and without opinions.
npc.native: Perché i numeri pari sono tristi. Io conto le persone sotto la pioggia, e mi piace un totale dispari, come nove o undici. Qual è il tuo numero preferito?
npc.translation: Because even numbers are sad. I count the people in the rain, and I like an odd total, like nine or eleven. What is your favourite number?

player: Sì, mi piace il pane! Ma non con la pioggia. Tu sei sempre qui, nel bosco?

npc.narrative: The pioggia taps on the lid of her ledger, which sits on a wobbly tavolo under a large cappello. Next to her stands a fila of one person, perfectly sicura of its place. She counts you, frowns, and writes a piccolo numero in the margin.
npc.native: Sì, sono sempre qui, anche quando piove. Faccio la fila anche da sola, perché una fila è una cosa seria. Il pane caldo è buono, ma il pane bagnato è triste. Dove mangi di solito la mattina?
npc.translation: Yes, I am always here, even when it rains. I form a queue even when I am alone, because a queue is a serious thing. Warm bread is good, but wet bread is sad. Where do you usually eat in the morning?

player: Va bene, devo andare. Grazie Tabitha, arrivederci!

npc.narrative: You step out into the pioggia, and Tabitha closes her libro with the care of someone sealing a will. Behind her a fila of one waits at the tavolo, which has no chairs and no complaints. Under the ombrello, the strada ahead shines like a freshly stamped form.
npc.native: Arrivederci, e grazie a te! Il tavolo per due resta prenotato, ma non chiedere come. Con te oggi passano undici persone, e undici è un numero dispari. Buona giornata, e porta l'ombrello!
npc.translation: Goodbye, and thanks to you! The table for two stays booked, but do not ask how. With you, eleven people pass today, and eleven is an odd number. Have a good day, and take the umbrella!
